ownerThemes.theme: Long-term owners call it the least finicky serger they have used: tension, length and differential are easy to adjust and fabric feeds straight rather than drifting before the needle.
Threading the lower looper is the one repeated complaint; owners with good eyesight say the lack of air threading is not a problem.

Versus the 654DE, the 644D puts the differential dial on the left and the stitch length control inside the door, lacks the lower looper lever, and needs a separate 2-thread converter; it is aimed at light to medium fabrics.
First-serger buyers weighing the 644D against the 654DE and the Brother 1034D are steered toward the 654DE if they can stretch the budget, or the 644D as the sturdier of the two cheaper options.

editorial.verdict: Juki's entry serger on paper: 2/3/4 thread, 1,500 spm, differential feed and a built-in rolled hem, with the 2-thread converter sold separately.
editorial.whoFor: A first-serger buyer who wants a Juki 2/3/4 thread machine with differential feed for light to medium fabrics and will buy the 2-thread converter only if needed.
editorial.skipIf: You want 2-thread stitches in the box, you need a published throat or free arm figure, or you plan to serge heavy layers all day.
editorial.keySpec: 2/3/4 thread · differential feed 0.7 to 2.0 · 1,500 spm · 15 lb
strengths: Juki publishes 1,500 spm, a 0.7 to 2.0 differential ratio and a built-in rolled hem that needs no needle plate change.
Owners report that threading is mostly manageable: 5 of 10 voices on threading and loopers were positive, and one retailer review says it arrived threaded.
Juki's catalog lists the 2/3 thread converter as optional here and standard on the MO-654DE, so the step-up difference is clear on paper.
weaknesses: 2-thread stitches need the optional converter, which is not in Juki's standard accessory list.
Owners report chain-stitch and lockup failures in some units; the reliability theme has 8 voices, split between praise and problems.
Juki does not publish throat space, stitch count or a thread trimmer, and its dial side and size documents disagree.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Juki MO-644D?
faqs.a: Owners are mixed but mostly kind. Threading draws the most comments, with some calling it manageable and others reporting thread breakage or chaining trouble, and build quality gets praise. Oiling and maintenance, tension and units that lock up draw the complaints. The read is thin, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki MO-644D and MO-654DE?
faqs.a: Juki's catalog lists the 2/3 thread converter as optional on the MO-644D and standard on the MO-654DE. The 654DE page also lists a lower looper threader, and it publishes 15.5 lb against the MO-644D's 15 lb. Juki prints a higher suggested retail price for the 654DE.

faqs.q: Does the Juki MO-644D do 2-thread stitches?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists 2/3/4 thread, but the catalog lists the 2/3 thread converter as optional and it is not in the standard accessory list, so 2-thread stitches need that converter.

faqs.q: Can the Juki MO-644D do a rolled hem?
faqs.a: Juki says rolled hemming is built in, set by a switch with no needle plate or foot change. Juki publishes a 2 mm rolled hem width; the rolled hem stitch length is not confirmed for this model [verify].

faqs.q: What is the price of the Juki MO-644D?
faqs.a: Juki prints a suggested retail price of $1,199 and tells buyers to contact an authorized dealer. Michaels showed $449 on 2026-09-29, a wide gap from list, so dealers set their own prices. Check what is in the box when you compare.

faqs.q: How do you thread the Juki MO-644D?
faqs.a: Juki describes color-coded guides, a manual lay-in path and a lower looper threaded through the front door, with a looper threader in the accessory list. Owners are split: 5 of the 10 voices on threading and loopers are positive and 2 are negative, and one retailer review says it arrived threaded. Follow the diagram in the manual, which is a related MO-644DN/654DEN edition.

faqs.q: What needles does the Juki MO-644D use?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists household HAx1 needles in sizes 11 to 14. The linked manual, a related MO-644DN/654DEN edition, names 130/705H, the same household family.

faqs.q: Is the Juki MO-644D good for beginners?
faqs.a: Owners report mixed experiences with threading: some call it easy and others had thread breakage or chaining trouble. Juki calls it easy to operate, which is a maker claim. A beginner should also price the optional 2-thread converter if 2-thread stitches matter.

faqs.q: How heavy is the Juki MO-644D?
faqs.a: Juki's page and catalog give 15 lb; the manual gives 7.0 kg. Juki's page gives 10.6 W x 13.5 H x 11.5 D in, while its catalog labels height and depth the other way round, so treat size as soft.
